transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-19
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Auriga Head of Search), Elena Rodriguez (Auriga ML), Tom Hart (Auriga CTO)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + rerank endpoints. Discussed typical latency/cost tradeoffs, instrumenting the Console, and initial pilot steps. Customer wants to validate relevance improvements vs their current ES + score boosting pipeline and check security posture for PII queries.

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Marcus, you okay to kick us off with a bit of context on where you are with search and what success looks like?

[00:00:12] Marcus: Yeah, sure, thanks Jordan. Um so quick backstory — we run a hybrid search stack, mostly Elastic, some FAISS for embeddings for long tail, but it's kinda brittle. Our product team sees mismatches in relevance and the QA team spends a lot of time tuning hand written rules. We're exploring hosted vector search plus rerank to reduce manual rules and improve MRR for discovery. Success for us is clear A/B win on NDCG and latency under 200ms P95 for the resolved endpoint. Also any solution needs to pass security review (SAML, KMS, audit logs).

[00:00:48] Jordan: Great, that's helpful. Priya, do you want to walk through what we'll demo today?

[00:00:52] Priya: Yeah quick agenda — 1) show Redwood Console, embeddings endpoint and batch flow, 2) reranking endpoint and example pipeline using our hosted API, 3) Optimize suggestions for batching/cache/quant profiles, and 4) Q/A and next steps. We'll keep it practical.

[00:01:08] Elena: Quick question — we're particularly sensitive about logs, so we're assuming hosted means Redwood sees tokenized payloads, right? How does that work with PII?

[00:01:16] Jordan: Good call. We often get that. For hosted we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, and we can purge logs or configure retention at the tenant level. We also have options for dedicated capacity or private VPC if you need no transit through our multi-tenant runtime. I'll share the security packet after.

[00:01:35] Tom: And SOC 2?

[00:01:37] Priya: Yep, SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs included. We also provide audit logs for API calls and model versions.

[00:01:45] Liam: Okay demo time — I'm going to share my screen, starting with the Console.

[00:01:51] [screen share noise]

[00:02:05] Liam: This is the Redwood Console project for embeddings. Top left you can see model catalog — we have several open-reach models and quantized variants. For embeddings we expose /v1/embeddings and you can choose dimension config and model family. I'm sending a sample request in the right panel — note you can stream step-by-step and batch requests.

[00:02:28] Marcus: When you say "dimension config" do you mean we can pick 384 vs 1024 vectors? We currently use 512.

[00:02:34] Priya: Exactly. Different models produce different dims; you can also use our projection config to normalize to your chosen dim, which helps pipeline compatibility with your FAISS or Pinecone index. There is a small compute cost for projection but it's usually worth the unified index approach.

[00:02:54] Elena: How do we handle incremental reindex? We can't re-embed millions each deploy.

[00:02:58] Liam: Two patterns — prefix cache for KV style caching and incremental backfill. Our Optimize module can recommend a cache window and batch size that balances latency. For reindexing we usually do prioritized backfill (hot docs first) — Redwood has a bulk embeddings job that runs in the background and reports progress.

[00:03:19] [00:03:20] Jordan: Let's move to rerank. The rerank endpoint accepts a query + top-K candidates and returns scores and optional re-written outputs. We'll show a small example where we take top 10 from Elastic, call /v1/rerank with context, and get re-ranked list with confidence.

[00:03:38] Liam: Sending a demo payload now — multishot example, you can see the request includes user query, top_k results and short passage text. The response returns a score vector and an explanation token list (sparse).

[00:03:55] Marcus: Does the reranker do cross-encoders or is it a lightweight model? Latency wise?

[00:04:02] Priya: We support multiple variants. Hosted default is a mid-size cross-encoder optimized for latency — it uses attention optimizations and caching to reduce repeated work. For very low latency we have a distilled reranker that scores faster. Typical P95 depends on length; for a 3-sentence passage and top-10 rerank we see 70–150ms on hosted with our smaller cross-encoder; heavier cross-encoders push higher but give slight quality gains.

[00:04:30] Elena: And cost? We're quoted per-token for generation, but rerank is per-call?

[00:04:36] Jordan: Rerank is priced per-document scored plus a small model unit. We'll send a tiered pricing sheet. For pilots we often credit the first 100k scored docs.

[00:04:45] [00:04:46] Marcus: Awesome. For our workflow we want to keep Elastic for recall and use rerank for final ordering, plus some feature signals from click logs. How do we pass signals?

[00:04:56] Liam: You can include numeric features in the rerank payload — click-through rate, recency score — and the reranker will incorporate them via a small feature head. We also support a lambda hook for server-side scoring enrichment if you need custom signals.

[00:05:12] Elena: Any gotchas with tokenization? We do some weird unicode emoji queries that break our current tokenizer.

[00:05:18] Priya: Tokenization differences can affect scoring; our Console shows token counts and you can choose tokenizer family to match your index. For odd inputs we recommend a cleanup preprocessor and we can share examples.

[00:05:28] [00:05:30] Jordan: Now I'll show the Optimize recommendations — here the platform analyzed a synthetic workload and suggested batching=16 for the embedding endpoint, cache TTL 5m for prefix hits, and quantized model for index building to reduce costs by ~40% with 3% quality delta.

[00:05:48] Marcus: Does Redwood do model quantization in hosted mode or do you provide quantized artifacts to us?

[00:05:54] Priya: Hosted runtime supports quantized execution paths; we also provide quantized export for Dedicated/Private if you want to run in-house. Quantization and KV cache options are surfaced in Optimize.

[00:06:07] Tom: For compliance, do you support customer-managed keys only in Private, or hosted as well?

[00:06:12] Jordan: Hosted supports customer KMS via cloud provider integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For stricter controls we recommend Dedicated or Private which can be in your VPC and integrate with on-prem HSMs.

[00:06:22] Elena: Any requirement on data residency? We're EU-first.

[00:06:25] Priya: You can pin region to EU nodes and we have data residency commitments in our enterprise terms.

[00:06:31] [00:06:35] Liam: Quick live hit — I'm going to run 3 queries from your sample logs (sanitized) and compare baseline Elastic ranking vs Redwood embeddings+rerank.

[00:06:42] [keyboard clacking noise]

[00:06:57] Liam: First query: "best beta blockers for arrhythmia" — Elastic baseline top result is a fairly generic doc. Our reranked top result surfaces a clinical guideline note, with a higher explain score. You can see the delta in NDCG here — small sample but directionally better.

[00:07:22] Marcus: Nice, that clinical doc is what product expects. What about P95?

[00:07:27] Priya: For this demo set the end-to-end P95 (Elastic + network + rerank) is ~180ms, within your 200ms SLO. If you need 100ms we'll discuss dedicated capacity and smaller rerank models.

[00:07:40] Elena: Can we run a head-to-head on our dataset?

[00:07:44] Jordan: Yes — that's the pilot: you give us a subset (10k queries and candidate pool) and we run a full bench and produce NDCG, latency, and cost per query. Priya will share the benchmark script.

[00:07:54] Marcus: On data sharing — we can't send PHI. Is there a way to mask or run on-prem?

[00:07:58] Priya: Two options — sanitize logs before upload, or run the pilot on Dedicated/Private in your VPC. For a quick eval many customers sanitize a sample. We'll document both flows.

[00:08:12] [00:08:15] Tom: For SLA and fallbacks — what happens if a model variant is overloaded?

[00:08:19] Liam: We have smart routing — requests can fall back to a cheaper model variant or a cached rerank if the cross-encoder is at capacity. You can configure fallbacks per route. We also expose per-route metrics in Console and provide alerts.

[00:08:33] Elena: Do you provide per-token cost visibility? Our finance team wants line items per model.

[00:08:38] Jordan: Yes Console shows token-level breakdown and cost by model and route. We'll attach a sample breakdown.

[00:08:45] [00:08:48] Marcus: Anything we should instrument on our side to make the pilot meaningful?

[00:08:51] Priya: Capture query text, user signals (clicks), candidate pool IDs, and latency SLOs. Also export a small set of labeled relevance judgments if you have them. That helps us tune reranker thresholds.

[00:09:04] Elena: Ok we do have a small labeled set for a subset of queries, I'll surface that.

[00:09:09] [00:09:12] Jordan: Cool, let's talk timeline — Jordan: We propose 2 week setup (access + sample upload), 2 week bench, then workshop to review.

[00:09:21] Marcus: That sounds reasonable. Budget wise — we're thinking pilot budget under $10k. Is that doable?

[00:09:28] Jordan: Definitely doable; we'll propose a pilot scope that fits that.

[00:09:33] [00:09:35] Liam: Quick detour on integration — API snippet: pull top_k from Elastic, call Redwood /v1/embeddings in batch (we recommend batching 16), then vector similarity, pass top 10 to /v1/rerank with features. We'll share sample client code in Python and Node.

[00:09:53] Elena: Any client libraries for streaming or retry logic?

[00:09:56] Priya: SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. Recommends exponential backoff, idempotency keys for bulk jobs, and circuit-breaker patterns.

[00:10:06] Tom: Do you support on-prem deployment if we decide later?

[00:10:09] Jordan: Yes — Redwood Private is available for enterprise customers, with a private control plane option and on-prem package. Migration is straightforward — same API surface.

[00:10:17] Marcus: Two final product-y questions: 1) can reranker return a short snippet rewrite for UI display? 2) do you surface explanation tokens for moderation?

[00:10:25] Priya: 1) Yes, reranker can return a condensed snippet field. 2) We return token-level saliency that can be used for moderation heuristics, but we recommend a separate moderation model for production-critical content.

[00:10:39] Elena: Are there any known mismatches with Elastic scoring we should watch for?

[00:10:43] Liam: Score calibration — when combining vector scores with Elastic BM25 you should normalize ranges. We provide calibrators and a small calibration job in the benchmark script.

[00:10:53] [sound of a chair]

[00:11:00] Jordan: OK let's recap next steps: 1) Jordan to send pilot proposal + pricing + security docs, 2) Priya to share benchmark scripts and demo artifacts, 3) Marcus/Elena to prepare sanitized sample logs and labeled set, target by 2027-04-22, 4) schedule kickoff — tentative 2027-04-26.

[00:11:22] Marcus: Great, will do. Quick ask — can you include a short checklist for the security team?

[00:11:28] Jordan: Yes I'll include a one pager with KMS flow, data retention, region pinning, and audit log samples.

[00:11:33] Tom: And pls include contact for legal procurement timelines.

[00:11:36] Jordan: Will include. Anything else?

[00:11:39] Elena: One last tiny thing — we sometimes get weird redirects or broken captions in our logs; can Priya share sample preprocessor script?

[00:11:45] Priya: Yep, small sanitize + tokenizer normalization script will be in the repo we share.

[00:11:52] [00:11:55] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.

[00:12:00] Marcus: Thanks everyone, excited to kick this off.

[00:12:04] [meeting ends — remaining ~30 mins were Q/A recorded in brief — transcript clipped for brevity but available in full note attachment]
notes: Customer is Auriga Systems, intent to run 4 week pilot. Main asks: pilot under $10k, EU data residency, KMS integration, sanitized logs for bench. Redwood to provide pricing, security docs, benchmark scripts, and sample SDKs. Next tentative kickoff 2027-04-26.
